div.head: I Cn 5.2a
div.ab: And gyf man freondleasne weofodþen mid tihtlan belecge, þe aðfultum næbbe, ga to corsnǽde ⁊ þær þonne æt gefare þæt þæt God wylle, buton he on husle geladian mote.
And gif man freondleasne weofodþen mid tihlan belecge, þe aðfultum næbbe, ga to corsnæde ⁊ þær þonne æt gefare þæt þæt God wille, buton he on husle geladian mote.

Si quis altari ministrantium accusetur et amicis destitutus consacramentales non habet, uadat ad iudicium quod Anglice dicitur corsnéd (id est panem coniuratum), et fiat sicut Deus uelit, nisi super (sanctum) corpus Domini permittatur ei se purgare (ut se purget).
And gyf man freondleasne weofodþen mid tihtlan belecge, þe aðfultum næbbe, ga to corsnǽde ⁊ þær þonne æt gefare þæt þæt God wylle, buton he on husle geladian mote.
And gyf man freondleasne weofodþen mid tihtlan belecge, þe aðfultum næbbe, ga to corsnæde, and þær þonne æt gefare þæt þæt God wylle, buton he on husle geladian mote.

Wenn ein Altardiener, der keine Freunde [und Sippe und daher] keine Eideshilfe besitzt, mit Anklage belegt wird, so schreite er zum [Ordal des] Entscheidungsbissens und erfahre [d. h. leide] dann dabei das, was Gott will, ausser wenn er Erlaubniss erhält, im Abendmahlsgenuss sich zu reinigen.

If a servant of the altar who has no friends [or kin, and so] no oath-helpers is charged with an accusation, let him go to the [ordeal of the] consecrated morsel, and then experience [i.e. suffer] there what God wills, unless he is permitted to clear himself by [taking] the sacrament.

And if an accusation is brought against a member of the priesthood who has no friends and no-one to support his oath, he shall go to the ordeal of consecrated bread, and shall experience there what is the will of God, unless he is allowed to clear himself by the Holy Communion.

And if an accusation is brought against a friendless cleric who serves at the altar, one who does not have supporters for his oath, he shall undergo the ordeal of consecrated bread, and there endure whatever God wills, unless he is permitted to exonerate himself by the sacrament.
